dimensions.assessment: Directly affects United States Capitol Police personnel, operators of unauthorized drones near the Capitol, and individuals whose drone communications might be intercepted.
dimensions.evidence: authorize personnel in the United States Capitol Police with assigned duties that include the security or protection of people, facilities, or assets to take... such actions

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes high-impact operational measures including seizing, disabling, or destroying drones and intercepting associated communications.
dimensions.evidence: Use reasonable force, if necessary, to disable, damage, or destroy the unmanned aircraft system.

dimensions.assessment: The source text does not state specific appropriations, funding amounts, or broader economic impacts.
Grants new security authorities and exceptions to multiple federal criminal and communications statutes specifically for the Capitol Police Board.
dimensions.evidence: Notwithstanding section 46502 of title 49, United States Code, or sections 32, 1030, and 1367 and chapters 119 and 206 of title 18

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing authorities and periodic reporting requirements, with termination tied to an existing provision in the Homeland Security Act of 2002.
dimensions.evidence: The authority to carry out this section... shall terminate on the date identified in section 210G(i) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002

missing_information: Specific cost figures for acquiring counter-drone technology and training.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill grants the Capitol Police Board authority to detect, track, disrupt, seize, or destroy unmanned aircraft systems posing threats to Capitol facilities and assets, subject to privacy rules and reporting requirements.
